title: MusicDET: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Music Detection
claim: Real data shows coherent, structured time-frequency energy patterns, while generated data shows irregular, inconsistent patterns that expose a systematic discrepancy.
layout: 2 spectrogram panels side by side, with a green zoomed inset on the right
description: Two magma-colored spectrograms sit side by side. Both have Time on the x-axis (ticks at 0 and 250) and Frequency on the y-axis (ticks at 0, 100 and 200). The left panel has smooth, diffuse energy that is concentrated at low frequencies. It shows a few faint curved harmonic lines and short bright horizontal dashes near the bottom. The right panel shows strongly banded horizontal stripes. It also has a sudden vertical break around time 250, after which there are wavy, fragmented streaks. A green box on the right panel marks a region, and green lines connect it to an enlarged inset on the far right. The inset shows jagged, irregular harmonic contours. The eye goes first to the bright right spectrogram and its green zoom inset. The panels have no titles or labels saying which is real and which is generated.
caption: Systematic discrepancies between real music and AI-generated music in terms of energy spectrograms. Real music exhibits coherent and well-organized time--frequency structures, whereas AI-generated music often displays irregular and less consistent spectral energy patterns.
abstract: Detecting AI-generated music is crucial for preserving artistic authenticity and preventing the misuse of generative music technologies. However, existing discriminative detectors typically rely on generated samples during training and often suffer from severe performance degradation when confronted with music produced by unseen generators, which limits their real-world applicability. To address this issue, we formulate a zero-shot setting for AI-generated music detection, where the detector is trained exclusively on real music without access to any generated samples. Under this setting, we propose MusicDET, a generator-agnostic detection framework based on frequency-guided normalizing flows that probabilistically models the distribution of real music features. By evaluating the likelihood of an input sample under the learned real-music distribution, MusicDET enables effective detection of out-of-distribution music signals. Experiments on the FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets show that MusicDET consistently outperforms conventional discriminative detectors, particularly when detecting music generated by previously unseen models.
